Rs_question: What is the average rate of formation of suitable stars (stars/year) in our galaxy?
fp_question: What fraction of stars form planets?
ne_param: number of habitable planets per star
ne_question: What is the average number of habitable planets per star?
fl_question: On what fraction of habitable planets does any form of life emerge?
fi_param: fraction of habitable planets with life that develop intelligence
fi_question: On what fraction of habitable planets with life does intelligence evolve?

intro_eq_body: In 1961, Frank Drake proposed an equation to estimate the number of detectable technological civilizations in the Milky Way. It multiplies seven parameters, each representing a step on the path from star formation to interstellar communication.
intro_eq_note: N = number of detectable civilizations in the Milky Way today
intro_why_body: The values ​​of the parameters are deeply uncertain and depend on very different areas of knowledge — astrophysics, biology, cognitive sciences. This survey seeks to capture the beliefs and uncertainties of the Brazilian astrobiological community in a quantitative way.
intro_step1: For each parameter, you will move a slider that defines a probability distribution—not a single value, but the range of values ​​you consider plausible and how likely each one is.
intro_step2: At the end, your personal distribution of N will be calculated and you can see how it compares to that of the community.
intro_step3: You can return later to view the aggregated results as more participants respond.
consent_what_body: This survey is conducted by researchers from [Institution] with the aim of quantifying the beliefs and uncertainties of experts about the parameters of the Drake Equation. The data will be used exclusively for academic purposes.
